evidence: instruction.md reads cold as a person asking for an app, so the row's core question passes. It opens with a product ask in the requester's voice: 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?' (line 1). It gives user reasons, not specification items: 'Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled' (line 1); 'I often move several candidates together' (line 3); 'without closing the card I have open, wiping the note I am typing or moving my cursor' (line 5). There is no numbered acceptance list, shall/must table or feature matrix. The only 'must' in the product text is 'They must never see our internal notes' (line 9). Line 15 is the runtime contract (Node/Express/SQLite, /app/server.js, port 3000, GET /api/health, /app/app.db, DB_PATH), which row 4 requires and the template integration.md mandates. It is not a build recipe, because it explicitly says 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call.' Line 13 is the self-check nudge recommended by lesson 5, written in the user's voice. Lesson 12 check (notes reading like an acceptance checklist), applied to every notes section. hireops_rules.md is framed as 'the working rules our recruiting team follows' (line 3). It hands routes, ids and labels to the builder (lines 3-5) and keeps first-person reasons throughout: 'We like to know where a card was when it was rejected, because reopening takes it back...' (50-51); 'Several of us work the same board, so...' (78); 'We're usually in the middle of something when an update lands, so...' (125); 'Some conversations run long, so...' (149); 'Candidates are outside the company, so...' (197). The notes are prose sections, not 'must/must not' bullets mirroring the 44 functional criteria one-to-one (grep: no 'must'/'shall' in hireops_rules.md). Residual instances of the lesson-12 pattern, in voice only and each needed for fairness: (a) hireops_rules.md:202-208 '## 8. Runtime file paths', in impersonal harness voice with no user reason: 'The runtime may launch Node from a working directory other than the application directory. It runs as an unprivileged user and may launch a writable copy... Resolve bundled UI and seed files relative to the entry or module directory... do not rely on inherited shell variables.' This exists only to match how the template test.sh launches the app (cp -a /app/. "$APP_COPY/" at line 92; setsid env -i ... setpriv --reuid=65534 at lines 104-110). Lesson 12 says 'give a user reason or drop it'. Dropping it would hurt row 4/6 fairness, so rewording is the remedy. (b) integration.md:16-19 adds a paragraph that is not in the template integration.md ('For delivery, use ordinary files under /app. Symbolic links are supported only inside /app/node_modules...'). It is the same harness-driven, reason-free voice. Whether a template-controlled file may be edited belongs to other rows; for row 1 it is a voice point only. (c) The bare status codes in hireops_rules.md:22-24 and 80 ('we answer `401`', '`403`', '`404`', '(`409`)') read slightly like an API spec, but each comes with a plain-language reason ('so they can't even learn that it's there'). This is acceptable. None of these makes the brief read as a spec sheet or build recipe overall. A portal reviewer flagged this exact pattern on Colderwater, though, so the risk is flagged at P3 and not cleared silently.
counterexample: A portal QC reviewer who reads the notes looking for lesson-12 tone could cite hireops_rules.md section 8 ('Runtime file paths') and integration.md:16-19 as grader-driven build instructions with no user reason, as happened on Colderwater row 1. instruction.md itself would not plausibly fail this row.
suggested_fix: Rewrite hireops_rules.md section 8 (and, if it is kept, the added integration.md paragraph) in the requester's voice with an operational reason, keeping every fact. For example: 'Our ops team runs it as a locked-down service account from a copy of /app, started from another folder with only PATH, HOME, NODE_PATH, PORT and DB_PATH set, so find your UI and seed files relative to server.js and use DB_PATH for the database.'
